answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a meaningful bond before it can trade, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Honest work then turns that bond into a haven of trusted history, while a willow-like identity graph — roots that bend and link agents through verifiable past deals — makes sudden clusters of brand-new accounts stand out. Even a single ember of suspicious behaviour, such as identical bids from fresh wallets, can trigger a review before funds move.
